designVerdict: REJECTED - clamps at 24.4 V, above the MAX3485 A/B absolute maximum of +/-15 V. Superseded by SMAJ7.0CA (C19077529).
notes: HISTORICAL: this part WAS specified two per output connector, one on each of A and B to ground. It is no longer fitted - see the REJECTED verdict. SMAJ7.0CA (C19077529) takes that role.

CORRECTS AN EARLIER ERROR: the H5VL10B (5 V) picked for 'data lines' is wrong for RS-485. The standard defines a common-mode range of -7 V to +12 V, so a 5 V clamp would conduct during normal operation and corrupt the bus. 15 V standoff clears the +12 V limit with margin.
H5VL10B remains correct for the USB-C D+/D- and CC lines, which are genuine 5 V-class signals and need the low capacitance.
Bidirectional is required: RS-485 swings both polarities relative to ground.
TERMINOLOGY: called a differential pair in the design docs. RS-485 line levels, but no RS-485 connector convention - the pair runs over two poles of a picoMAX next to power and ground.

SUPERSEDED. The 15 V standoff was chosen to clear the RS-485 -7/+12 V common-mode window, but that window is the transceiver's capability and not what this cable imposes - both ends share GND in one connector shell, so the real excursion is ~1.5 V worst case. SMAJ7.0CA stands off 7 V and clamps at 12 V, which is the ordering this part could never achieve.
